newsitem.title: USA: CBOT wheat closes lower on fund selling, weather.
newsitem.headline: CBOT wheat closes lower on fund selling, weather.

text.p: CBOT wheat futures closed lower with the market pressured late by small-lot fund selling amid a near dearth of buying interest, traders said.
"O'Brien, Man, and CIS sold it late, it was just some fund liquidation. There was just nothing else in here," a trader said.
Traders said forecasts for weather considered conducive for the U.S. winter wheat crop may have hit the market, the traders said.
Wheat early was supported by export numbers but even that data failed to stir substantial bullish momentum.
USDA Friday said U.S. net export sales of wheat during the week ended December 19 totaled 353,200 tonnes, above the range of trade estimates for 200,000 to 300,000 tonnes.
There also were diminished fears about wet-weather related losses in Argentina's wheat growing region.
However, traders in Buenos Aires said Argentine cash wheat was firm early Friday on forecasts for rain this weekend in key southern grain areas, which could lead to harvest delays.
Wheat closed unchanged to 4-1/2 cents per bushel lower, with March down 4-1/2 at $3.89-1/2.
Wheat futures volume was estimated at 6,000 contracts, about the same as the 6,059 traded Thursday, according to the CBOT.
In wheat options, LFG Futures sold 125 July $3.70 calls at 11-1/2 cents, Term Commodities sold 100 March $4.00 calls at 11-1/2 and sold 100 March $3.80 puts at seven cents.
Wheat options volume was estimated at 2,000 contracts, slightly below the 2,143 traded Thursday.
